title: From agent to service
summary: The support agent becomes a service: built once at start-up with a checkpointer, called over HTTP with typed requests and meaningful errors, streamed as typed events, protected from blocking calls and bursts, with conversations that survive a restart, and slow work moved to background jobs in Redis.
learn: **Serving an agent**: built once, a thread per conversation, JSON and streamed endpoints
**Typed, honest APIs**: 422 before any model call, 503 with Retry-After when the provider is down, /health
**Streaming typed events** (tool, tool_result, token, done), and **stopping when the client leaves**
**Async and concurrency**: ainvoke, a semaphore for the provider, a time budget (504)
**Conversations in Postgres**, and **background jobs** with RQ: 202, poll, retries
flow:
website backend ─(X-API-Key, X-Customer-ID)→ POST /agent/chat[/stream]
   → slot (semaphore) → time budget → agent.ainvoke / astream (thread = customer:thread_id, checkpoints in Postgres)
   → reply | events: tool → tool_result → token… → done
POST /reports → 202 + job id ──→ Redis ──→ RQ worker ──→ GET /reports/{id}

labs.explain:
Two turns on one thread through **POST /agent/chat** (the follow-up needs the first turn), and the thread read back from the checkpointer.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The agent **built once** for five requests, four bad requests refused **before any model call**, a provider outage as **503 with Retry-After**, the health check, and a test through **ASGITransport**.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

The support agent **streamed** from a real server as typed events (tool, tool_result, token, done) read with **httpx-sse**; then a client that **leaves after two tokens**, and a run that stops with it.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Six requests at once, each needing a 1-second model call: a **blocking** endpoint, an **async** one, and one limited to **two model calls at a time**; then a **time budget** (504).

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

One conversation with a **restart** in between, with the **in-memory** checkpointer and with **AsyncPostgresSaver**. Needs `docker compose up -d`.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Postgres checkpoints, opened in the lifespan.

labs.explain:
**POST /reports** answers 202 at once; an **RQ worker** builds the weekly digest while the client polls; a **flaky job** retried until it succeeds. Needs `docker compose up -d` (Redis).

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

path.title: Production path: the support agent as a service
path.summary: The Nimbus API serves the support agent: one agent built at start-up with Postgres checkpoints, threads namespaced by customer, a semaphore and a time budget around every run, typed events streamed until the client leaves, and the weekly digest as a background job.

steps.title: Service
steps.explain: AgentService.start builds the agent with its checkpointer in the lifespan; ask() takes a slot, sets a time budget and maps provider failures to 503/502.
production: agent_concurrency stays below the provider's limit; agent_timeout_s below the load balancer's.

steps.title: Stream
steps.explain: stream() turns agent.astream(updates, messages) into tool, tool_result, token and done events; the run lives in its own task, cancelled the moment the client leaves.
production: Without it, a client that leaves doesn't stop the run: under Starlette's anyio cancellation LangGraph can't clean up.

steps.title: Memory
steps.explain: agent_checkpointer=postgres keeps every thread in the course database; thread ids are namespaced by customer, so a customer can only read their own.

steps.title: Jobs
steps.explain: POST /reports enqueues weekly_digest and answers 202; workers run it; retries with intervals need --with-scheduler.
production: Run workers as their own deployment, scaled on queue length (Production track).

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Two conversations whose second turn only makes sense with the first, each streamed on a real server and continued after a restart, with each checkpointer.

| | follow-ups right after a restart | first streamed event (p50) |
|---|---|---|
| checkpointer: memory | 0/2 | 3.1 s |
| **checkpointer: postgres** | **2/2** | **1.6 s** |

Each second turn ("How much did it cost?", "When was it delivered?") only makes sense with the first ("my order NC-20417", "my oldest order"). After a restart the in-memory checkpointer had forgotten the thread and both follow-ups missed the right fact; with Postgres both did. Streaming the same runs also showed the service stopping work when a client leaves: after a client disconnected at word 2, the model produced 2 words, not 15. That needed the run in its own task (`streaming.in_own_task`); with Starlette's cancellation alone the run kept going.
production: Run it against every deployment: a restart must never lose a conversation.
